candidates.description: The developer said growth came entirely from sustenance sales, while collections rose 67 per cent and two Mahim projects worth over ₹4,100 crore are lined up

The Mumbai-based developer said in a stock exchange filing on Monday that the growth was driven by sustenance sales, as it did not launch any new projects during the quarter, along with steady price realisation in its existing premium residential portfolio, Address by GS, and homebuyer confidence in its projects. The company had reported pre-sales of ₹3,023 crore in FY26 and ₹700 crore in Q1FY27. Raymond Realty’s collections during Q2FY27 rose 67 per cent YoY to ₹682 crore. article.title: Mono Rail Projects
article.description: Guide to monorail in India — the Mumbai Monorail (MMRDA), how straddle-beam monorail works, shelved projects and the latest news.
article.postedBy: Metro, RRTS & High-Speed Rail Project Updates
article.sourceName: Metro, RRTS & High-Speed Rail Project Updates
article.articleTextExcerpt: A monorail runs on a single elevated beam rather than a conventional two-rail track. That makes it a compact, fully elevated mode, useful on dense urban corridors where road space is tight. In India the flagship is the Mumbai Monorail, the country’s first and so far only system. This page covers monorail in India: how the technology works, where it runs, and the latest developments. A monorail vehicle straddles or hangs from a single guideway beam, usually on rubber tyres. The result is a small footprint, a tight turning radius and a quiet ride. Most modern systems, Mumbai’s included, use the straddle-beam design, where the train sits astride a slim concrete beam. On capacity it sits below metro. It works well as a feeder or on medium-demand corridors, but it cannot match a metro’s throughput, which is why cities weigh it carefully against light metro and Metrolite. The Mumbai Monorail is India’s first and only monorail, running 19.54 km between Chembur and Sant Gadge Maharaj Chowk (Jacob Circle) under the Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority (MMRDA), serving eastern and central Mumbai neighbourhoods that the metro and suburban rail do not reach directly. It has brought forward that the proportion of households consuming iodised salt has dropped from 94.9 per cent in the last survey to 88.7 per cent. Iodised salt is a critical source of iodine, a trace mineral required for the production of thyroid hormones that regulate growth, metabolism and development. Public health experts warn that the decline in usage could reverse decades of progress made under India’s Universal Salt Iodisation (USI) programme, which was introduced to combat iodine deficiency disorders. The growing popularity of sendha namak (rock salt) and other speciality variants has contributed to the decline. “While these alternatives are often marketed as ‘natural’ or ‘pure’ but they lack adequate iodine content. Sendha namak may be used occasionally, but relying on it exclusively for daily cooking deprives the body of essential iodine,” said Dipti, a nutritionist. As part of the launch, Leo Energies has signed agreements to acquire around 650 MWp of solar capacity across Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, Gujarat, Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh. All the projects are expected to be operational at the time of acquisition and are backed by long-term power purchase agreements (PPAs) with central offtakers, state discoms and commercial and industrial customers. In addition, around 160 MWp of generation capacity and 50 MWh of battery energy storage capacity have already been acquired and closed. This includes 110 MWp of generation capacity and 50 MWh of BESS acquired from TrueRE Oriana Power. The platform also has further acquisitions and greenfield PPA auctions in sight as part of its near-term pipeline.

article.articleTextExcerpt: Construction 1 min read Trichy civic body warns builders over illegal construction & demolition waste dumping The civic body will penalise builders dumping construction materials on roads and disrupting traffic in areas including Thennur and Vayalur Road, while a C&D waste recycling unit is planned at Panjapur. TNN Published On Oct 2, 2026 at 02:35 PM IST Representative AI imageTrichy Corporation Commissioner N Ponmalai on Thursday warned builders and construction companies against dumping construction and demolition (C&D) waste on roads and near water bodies, following complaints from residents that such dumping was affecting vehicular movement.The commissioner said the corporation would levy on-the-spot penalties, as per its bylaws, against those continuing to dispose of C&D waste illegally.Dumping of construction materials and debris on roads has caused traffic bottlenecks in several parts of the city, including Thennur, Vayalur Road and Uyyakondan aqueduct bund roads. The corporation also said temporary shelters for storing construction materials or accommodating workers should be confined to the private property where construction is under way and should not encroach on roads.

postedNews.title: Gaur Alaris Sells Out Entire Inventory in 48 Hours, Reaching Sales of Rs 1800 Crore
postedNews.description: Delhi NCR, October 5, 2026: Gaurs Group has completely sold out its newly launched premium residential project, Gaur Alaris, located in Sector 22D along the

The 11.8-acre development, comprising approximately 1,088 3-BHK and 4-BHK apartments in its first phase, generated Rs 1800 crore in sales, nearing its estimated realization target of Rs 1,900 crore set during its initial August 2026 launch. postedNews.articleTextExcerpt: DLF Sells 172 Senior Living Homes in Gurugram for Rs 1,985 Crore DLF has completed the sale of all 172 homes at its newly launched senior living project, The Aureva, in Gurugram. The project has recorded sales of around Rs 1,985 crore, with the units sold at Rs 28,000 per sq ft. The company announced the complete sell-out of the project through a regulatory filing. The Aureva spans 4.17 acres in Sector 63, Gurugram. DLF said the project has achieved sales of about Rs 1,985 crore, reflecting strong demand for thoughtfully planned luxury retirement communities that combine luxury, wellbeing, convenience, healthcare access and community engagement.
